key_highlights: ASX records fourth consecutive losing week as rising bond yields pressure equities
RBA signals continued rate hikes despite sharp unemployment jump, creating an 'interest rate pincer' for households
AUD experiences sharp depreciation ('trapdoor opens') amid US-China geopolitical escalation
Australian house prices over halfway to largest 40-year decline, with Victoria worst-hit
Junior mining sector active: gold exploration hits (Aurum, Zenith, Auric) and Rio2 copper drilling in Peru
$2.7B cap raise wave pressures junior ASX miners; Star casino licence suspension weighs on gaming
Over half of Australian renters financially stressed; consumer confidence deteriorating

sectors.trend: Exploration activity robust with multiple high-grade gold hits (Aurum 155g/t, Zenith 6/6 in WA, Auric beyond Munda pit) and Rio2 copper drilling in Peru. However, $2.7B cap raise wave signals capital stress in juniors. Iron ore/coal exposed to US-China tensions.
sectors.implications: Large-caps (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) face headwinds from China demand uncertainty. Junior gold miners (AUR.AX, ZEN.AX, AURC.AX) offer speculative upside but cap raises dilute shareholders. Selective exposure to gold as inflation hedge warranted.

sectors.trend: RBA hawkish stance supports net interest margins but rising unemployment threatens credit quality. Renters' financial stress (59) and house price declines (45) elevate NPL risk. Star casino licence suspension (27) pressures gaming-linked lending.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher rates short-term but face provisioning headwinds within 6-12 months as unemployment bites. Defensive positioning in large-cap banks preferred over ASX200 peers.

sectors.trend: Data centre boom straining energy supply (53), creating structural demand but also price volatility. Russia-Ukraine strikes (8) support oil/gas prices. LNG and coal exporters face China demand uncertainty.
sectors.implications: SAP.AX, WES.AX, AGL.AX benefit from sustained energy demand. Coal/LNG names (BHP.AX, WDS.AX) volatile on geopolitical headlines. Energy infrastructure plays gain from data centre buildout.

sectors.trend: Severe consumer stress: interest rate pincer, renter hardship, house price declines. Star casino suspension (27) hits gaming. Property sector weak with CBD tower sales at fire-sale prices (46).
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX, CSG.AX face margin pressure. REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) pressured by falling property values and rising rates. Defensive consumer staples preferred over discretionary.

sectors.trend: Medicare breach (25) and AI safety concerns (4, 36, 63) create regulatory overhang. Global AI chip race (64-70) positive for tech sentiment but limited ASX direct exposure. CSL.AX remains defensive anchor.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, WES.AX (pharma) offer defensive quality. ASX tech names limited; global AI trade (NVDA, AMD) provides indirect sentiment support. Regulatory risk to digital health.

key_themes: RBA hawkish pivot vs. deteriorating labour market creates policy dilemma
AUD depreciation cycle opens import-cost inflation risk
House price correction enters advanced stage (40-year high decline)
Bond yield escalation threatens equity valuations ('will bonds crash stocks')
Geopolitical escalation (US-China, Russia-Ukraine) drives commodity volatility
Junior mining cap raise wave signals capital market stress
Consumer financial stress broadening across renters and fixed-rate holders

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA continued hikes amid rising unemployment
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight rate-sensitive defensives (CSL.AX, WES.AX); underweight growth and REITs; monitor RBA statement for pivot signals
Hedge AUD exposure; favour export-oriented miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX) and domestic consumption plays; avoid import-heavy retailers
Reduce REIT and property-linked exposure; monitor bank NPL provisions; favour fixed-income over property
Maintain commodity hedges; diversify away from China-exposed iron ore/coal; hold gold as safe haven

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Bond yield spike crashing equity valuations
risk_assessment.mitigation: Shorten duration in growth stocks; favour cash-flow-positive large caps; monitor 10-yr GBA yield
Avoid pre-announcement cap raise names; favour funded explorers with limited dilution risk

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold-exposed miners as inflation/geopolitical hedge
opportunities.rationale: Multiple high-grade hits (Aurum, Zenith, Auric) signal sector strength; AUD weakness and geopolitical risk support gold pricing

opportunities.recommendation: Position in large-cap diversified miners for AUD hedge and commodity exposure
opportunities.rationale: AUD depreciation boosts AUD-reported earnings; copper drilling (Rio2) signals structural demand; gold diversification within BHP/RIO

opportunities.recommendation: Defensive tilt to healthcare and consumer staples
opportunities.rationale: Rate pincer and unemployment stress favour essential spending; CSL provides dividend stability amid market volatility

defensive_moves.rationale: 40-year house price decline underway; CBD property fire-sale pricing signals structural oversupply; rising rates compress valuations

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim growth/tech exposure; increase cash or short-duration bonds
defensive_moves.rationale: Fourth consecutive ASX losing week; bond yields climbing; 'will bonds crash stocks' risk elevated; RBA not yet pivoting

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid junior miners with pending cap raises
defensive_moves.rationale: $2.7B cap raise wave creates dilution overhang; brokers under pressure; select only well-funded names

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. Fourth consecutive losing week likely to continue as RBA maintains hawkish bias despite unemployment spike. AUD weakness and rising bond yields create headwinds. Expect ASX200 to test lower supports. Volatility elevated on geopolitical headlines.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive by 6-12 months if RBA pivots on sustained unemployment deterioration. House price correction nearing completion offers eventual property rebound. Commodity super-cycle (copper, gold) supports miners. Consumer recovery contingent on rate cuts.
key_catalysts: RBA cash rate decision and statement (hawkish hold vs. pivot)
AUD/USD trajectory and RBA intervention risk
US-China trade/geopolitical escalation impact on iron ore demand
Australian house price data (CoreLogic, SQM) confirming 40-year decline depth
Unemployment rate trend and RBA response
Junior miner cap raise announcements and ASX20 liquidity
Russia-Ukraine conflict escalation and energy pricing

Iron ore (62% Fe) and copper spot prices
ASX200 and S&P/ASX 200 sector rotation (financials vs. materials)
CoreLogic house price index (national and Sydney/Melbourne)
Unemployment rate and labour force participation
China PMI and property sector data
ASX20 cap raise volume and dilution metrics
Star casino licence resolution and gaming sector impact
